Children have a wonderful way of seeing the world through imagination, turning ordinary encounters into extraordinary adventures. snippet.title: What it’s really like in San Quentin, one of America’s most notorious prisons
snippet.description:
W. Kamau Bell goes behind the walls of San Quentin, one of America's most notorious prisons, to meet the men inside. Hear from people who have spent most of their lives behind bars and see who they've become.

In W. Kamau Bell's own words: "I had a great time in prison. That’s something I never thought I’d say... Admittedly, I had a great time in prison at San Quentin because every night I was allowed to leave and go home. I didn’t have to live in the cramped cells. I didn’t have to figure out ways to navigate the horrible – and I mean horrible – food. I was able to focus instead on the men who I met there. They were all funny, smart, remorseful, resourceful, skilled and self-reflective in ways that most people that I meet on the outside are not."

Originally broadcast in April 2016.

Henüz genç yaşlarda olmasına rağmen önceliğini maddi kazanca değil, sahada kendisini gösterebilmeye veren Arda'nın bu isteği futbolseverlerin dikkatini çekiyor.

snippet.description:
What would you tell an alien civilisation about life on Earth?

In 1977, a once-in-a-lifetime alignment of the planets gave Nasa the chance to launch spacecraft that could explore the outer edges of our solar system and beyond. Onboard was a gold-plated record carrying sounds, music and pictures of Earth, designed as a message for any aliens that might be out there. As the Voyager 1 probe reaches the milestone of one light-day from Earth, we explore the extraordinary story of the Golden Record. We look at how an alien civilisation might decode it, what its message reveals about humanity and how its map could point extraterrestrials back to our planet.

snippet.title: AIの謎表現は、どこから来たのか？【学習データではない】
snippet.description:
AIが使う独特の言葉はどこから来た？ その言葉づかい、もう僕らの喋りにもうつっているかもしれません。

【目次】
0:00 AIっぽい言葉はどこから来た？
4:40 RLHFのせい
10:42 ラテン語由来の語が流行る？
12:47 「落ちる」を使うAI
17:42 人間の喋りもAIに引っ張られる
20:32 AIからうつった語彙「手番」
24:38 AIで方言はどう変わる？
27:57 AIっぽい日本語は嫌われる
30:53 増えた原因はあくまで仮説
32:04 みんなの「AIの口癖」を募集します

【参考文献】
◯PubMed「Delving into LLM-assisted writing in biomedical publications through excess vocabulary」 ( https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40601754/ )
→論文に「delve」が増えた話や、その分析。

◯ACL Anthology「Why Does ChatGPT “Delve” So Much? Exploring the Sources of Lexical Overrepresentation in Large Language Models」 ( https://aclanthology.org/2025.coling-main.426/ )
→delveなど一部語彙の過剰使用について、RLHFが怪しいんじゃないか、みたいなことを言ってる研究。

◯arXiv「Word Overuse and Alignment in Large Language Models: The Influence of Learning from Human Feedback」 ( https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.01930 )
→上の論文の続きっぽいやつ。LlamaのBase版とInstruct版の語彙を比較。

◯arXiv「Empirical evidence of Large Language Model's influence on human spoken communication」 ( https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.01754v3 )
→ChatGPTが多用する語彙が、人間の話し言葉でも増えていることを示した研究。

◯Nature「AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data」 ( https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-07566-y )
→「モデル崩壊」の話はここから。

◯Meta AI「Llama 3.2: Revolutionizing edge AI and vision with open, customizable models」 ( https://ai.meta.com/blog/llama-3-2-connect-2024-vision-edge-mobile-devices/ )
→Llama 3.2の事後学習が、教師あり微調整・棄却サンプリング・直接選好最適化を含むことを説明する公式資料。

◯太平記 ( https://w.wiki/dgGc )

◯家 ( https://www.aozora.gr.jp/cards/000158/files/1509_40739.html )
